nameOrigin.text: The city bears the name of Lancaster Lupton, a former lieutenant in the U.S. Dragoons who began building a trade fort here in 1836.

timeline.text: Lancaster Lupton began building a trade fort for the fur and buffalo hide trade with the plains tribes. It operated as Fort Lancaster until 1844.
The Fort Lupton Library, now the Fort Lupton City Museum building, was built by architect John J. Huddart.
The last wall of the original fort was demolished by workers erecting gas and oil drilling rigs on the site.
The South Platte Valley Historical Society was started with the aim of rebuilding the fort.
The reconstructed Fort Lancaster was completed and dedicated.
